subject: GRB 260710A: SVOM/GRM observation
body:
SVOM/GRM team: Xue-Yuan Zao, Chen-Wei Wang, Shi-Jie Zheng, Yue Huang, Shao-Lin Xiong, Shuang-Nan Zhang (IHEP)

SVOM/ECLAIRs team: Olivier Godet, Sebastien Guillot (IRAP)

Report on behalf of the SVOM team:

SVOM/GRM was triggered on-ground and in-flight by GRB 260710A at 2026-07-10T12:58:43.450 UTC (T0), which is also detected by Fermi/GBM (Fermi GBM team, GCN #45131 and M. Dafcikova et al., GCN #45138).

With the event-by-event data downloaded through the X-band ground station, we conducted the standard analysis pipeline of GRB 260710A. The GRM light curve shows that this burst consists of a single pulse with a T90 of 2.60 +1.00/-0.60 s in the 15-5000 keV band. 

The SVOM/GRM light curve can be found here：
https://www.bursthub.cn/gcn/2026/svgrb260710A.png

In addition, the position of this burst, as determined by Fermi/GBM (RA= 5.6, DEC=-85.0, ERR= 1.8 degrees, GCN #45131), is located at about 60 degrees from the SVOM optical axis, which is outside the ECLAIRs field of view.

With this localization, the time-averaged spectrum from T0-0.25 to T0+2.75 s is best fitted by a power law function with an exponential high-energy cutoff. The power law index is -1.27 +/-0.12 and the cutoff energy, parameterized as Epeak, is 161 +41/-25 keV. The event fluence (10-1000 keV) in this time interval is (2.26 +0.21/-0.17) E-06- erg/cm^2. 

The 1s peak spectrum, measured from T0-0.05 to T0+0.95 s, is also fitted by a power law function with an exponential high-energy cutoff, the power law index is -0.91 +/- 0.10 and the cutoff energy, parameterized as Epeak, is 153 +16/-12 keV. The flux (10-1000 keV) in this time interval is (1.74 +0.09/-0.08) E-06 erg/cm^2/s.

The localization of GRB 260710A in the 'Amati' relation diagram is shown at: 
https://www.bursthub.cn/gcn/2026/svgrb260710A_amati.png

The localization of GRB 260710A in the 'Yonetoku' relation diagram is shown at: 
https://www.bursthub.cn/gcn/2026/svgrb260710A_yonetoku.png

The Space Variable Objects Monitor (SVOM) is a China-France joint mission led by the Chinese National Space Administration (CNSA, China), National Center for Space Studies (CNES, France) and the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS, China), which is dedicated to observing gamma-ray bursts and other transient phenomena in the energetic universe. GRM is developed by the Institute of High Energy Physics (IHEP) of CAS.

The SVOM/GRM point of contact for this burst is: Xue-Yuan Zao (IHEP) (zaoxy@ihep.ac.cn)
